primary_board.content: Actual Blender-rendered v029/v030 contact,loaded-down,passing,up close and shot-camera comparisons

contact_upper_body_scanline.scope: Pixel-size preservation/readability check only, not artistic acceptance

observed_improvements: Shoulder/ribcage envelope is visibly fuller around the unchanged head.
Contact/down differ through whole-body mass, not just head/knee.
Knee edges are softer; useful passing leg separation retained.
Passing boot projects clear of support ankle more clearly without increasing minimum sole clearance.
Up combines forefoot roll, extended support and pelvis/ribcage rise.
Rear contact hand separates from hem; front gestures hang more calmly.
remaining_art: Coat/ribcage still reads as broad armor-like graphic planes.
Pelvis value bridge may still look like a patch rather than mass.
Passing/up hands partly merge with hem or thigh.
The loaded-down may overstate crouching/fatigue; four static drawings cannot settle this.
Body surface is a structural value block-in against retained painted head/collar/boots.
review.independent_review_routing: Through parent, as requested; no direct cross-thread review message attempted.

not_an_art_pass: The volume/projection corrections are visible, but the broad graphic coat, pelvis value bridge and hand staging still need independent review. Stronger load/rise could become crouched/bouncy if generically interpolated.
travel_contract: None authored. Root/stage frozen. Frames1,4,11,13 select independent poses; timing/intermediate playback undefined.
head_choice: Original painted profile/head/hair UVs and design retained, translated with the revised whole-body mass positions; no turnaround or v008 patch.
coordination: All short threads2 Blender jobs used immediate host no-Blender-process gates and exited. No heavy/full-cycle render. Per user instruction, review requests go through parent; no direct world message attempted.
remaining_review_request: Please independently review the v030 board before any full-cycle work, focusing on body/head proportion, loaded body mass, the boot/ankle gap and UP support construction.
